item.title: Immersion breaker
item.content:encoded:
I agree with Dr Poke that the last two sentences in the letter make no sense.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Damn, glad I found this! I clicked randomly on a Series I article and here I am! I like history-based SCPs but more recent events are pretty eh for me. However, this strikes all the right chords for me. The lives of men washed down the gutter of history in a forgotten battle with old-fashioned anomalous inventors. Being from the Balkans, I do find the stuff about Austria-Hungary very interesting and I'm glad I found it here. The way you show the two scientists, particularly Durand, is pretty chill-inducing. You start us out thinking Nemeş is the obvious bad guy and the slow reveal of the shit Durand did "for peace" really speaks of the way evil can hide behind a facade of peace-keeping and good intentions. In the end, he used the weapons that should never have been used "to test them". In the end, those who come out on top in war rarely have peaceful intentions.

I'm glad this was written so I could read it! I'll try to translate it one day.

+1

You don't really need to cease life function if every cell was completely obliterated.

If every cell was completely obliterated, you'd cease life functions. If a cell was obliterated, it would cease life functions.

The article states that the cells cannot cease life function. Ergo, the cells are still alive, despite being ash. Same with the person.

Fortunately for the incinerated, conciousness and thought processes seems to stem from neurological connections, which would be destroyed by incineration!

Wait…

The rest of the soldier's head was now gone, and the screaming was replaced by some sort of low grunting, the likes of which I have never heard from men.

Love this, because I love World War I. But:

Mortar shells specially designed to be fired from a Mortier de 58mm type 2, containing a gas that causes animal cells to become unable to cease life function.

I don't get this. At all, I mean. This is basically the cure to… death, right? So why would the Frenchman, and I'm assuming that his intentions actually were good, go to the military with this instead? And wouldn't this, in many cases, work against their side? Shoot a guy's leg, gets shot off, he shoots you in the stomach, screaming in agony. It's counterproductive. So, that's a nitpick that really bothers me here. It's essentially the Fountain of Youth, just aerosolized and canistered.

item.title: Wow.
item.content:encoded:
I'm in total agreement. The mental image of a man with half his head blown off still alive and screaming is just amazing, but the fact that the only reservation that the higher-ups had was the efficacy, rather than the cruelty of the weapons is what really sealed this. The real horror isn't the weapon itself, it the fact that they would actually deploy it.

Anyone can write an SCP that does horrible things to people, not many people can really touch the banality of evil like this did.

Upvoted.

item.title: Metadata
item.content:encoded:
For the record, I've identified the man whose photo is used in this SCP. This is Mészöly Géza, a Hungarian soldier (as per Hungarian naming practices, "Mészöly" was his family name and "Géza" was his personal name). Géza was a participant in the 1912 Olympics in Stockholm (shooting, military rifle). He was born in 1876, and was killed in 1919, during a skirmish pertaining to the short-lived Hungarian Soviet Republic.

Picture was originally posted here - http://www.flickr.com/photos/37578663@N02/7073280231 - by Flickr user Elinor04, who identifies Géza as "my grandfather's cousin".
